## Context
Project guidance currently describes `--force` and equivalent reason-bearing force parameters as human escape hatches, but it does not categorically prohibit agents from invoking them. Agents must stop and escalate to the user whenever an operation would require bypassing a configured gate or policy. Escalation does not authorize the agent to perform the override; the human operator must decide and execute any force operation.

## Scope
Update only the canonical contributor/agent guidance in `AGENTS.md`. Preserve the command documentation needed for human operators while making the agent prohibition and escalation requirement unambiguous. No runtime enforcement or other documentation changes are part of this task.

## Plan
1. Add a concise, prominent rule near the existing claim and force-escape-hatch guidance.
2. Cover the actual force surface: CLI `--force` / `--force=<reason>` and equivalent reason-bearing force parameters on library or MCP operations, including when the same transition force option targets close. Do not refer to the retired `--force-close` spelling as a live option.
3. Require agents to stop, report the blocking condition, and ask the user to decide and perform the human-controlled next step. State that user escalation never permits the agent itself to invoke the force override.
4. Verify the literal prohibition and escalation language with focused searches, inspect the one-file diff, run `git diff --check`, and run the repository lint gate.

## Testing
- `rtk grep -n -E "MUST NOT.*force|must never.*force" AGENTS.md` proves a categorical agent prohibition is present.
- `rtk grep -n -E "stop.*user|escalat.*user|user.*perform" AGENTS.md` proves the human escalation path is present.
- `rtk grep -n -- "--force-close" AGENTS.md` must not introduce the retired spelling as a live option.
- `rtk git diff --check` must pass.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` must pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `AGENTS.md` explicitly prohibits agents from invoking CLI `--force` / `--force=<reason>` or passing an equivalent force parameter through library or MCP operations.
- [x] The guidance requires the agent to stop, report the blocker, and escalate to the user whenever progress would depend on a force override.
- [x] The guidance states that escalation does not authorize the agent to run the override; any force operation is a human-operator action.
- [x] Existing human-operator escape-hatch documentation remains accurate and clearly distinguished from prohibited agent behavior.
- [x] No files outside `AGENTS.md` are intentionally modified.
- [x] The focused searches, `git diff --check`, and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` pass.
